title: How induction of labour scheduling shapes delay, workload and women's experience: an interpretive description study
abstract: Aim: to understand how staff across the booking chain and women experience the scheduling and starting of induction of labour, and where delay and unsafe workload arise. Design: qualitative interpretive description with interviews and focus groups. Setting: one labour and birth unit. Results will follow analysis.
introduction: Induction of labour is increasing, and fixed booking slots meet fluctuating labour ward capacity. Existing studies describe clinicians' and women's accounts but not those of booking and bed management staff.
methods: Purposive sampling of midwives, obstetricians, coordinators, booking clerks, bed managers and women with a delayed induction; semi-structured interviews and focus groups; reflexive thematic analysis mapped to booking steps with SEIPS.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present themes by booking step and the redesign recommendations.
discussion: The discussion will compare the findings with the retrieved qualitative and unit data studies and with the unchecked leads once they are retrieved.
limitations: One unit; insider researcher; retrospective accounts.
summary: Qualitative report structure with results left empty.
